INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.error: Says an atom and a molecule are the same.

example.question: What is a molecule?
example.wrong_answer: The smallest particle of an element
example.correct_answer: Two or more atoms joined together

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.cause: Hears both words used for "a tiny particle" and has never seen atoms joined into a molecule.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.reveals: Offer "The smallest particle of an element" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.help: Build an oxygen molecule from two balls.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.feedback: An atom is one particle. A molecule is two or more atoms joined.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.error: Says a compound is made of one kind of atom.

example.question: What is a compound?
example.wrong_answer: A substance made of one kind of atom
example.correct_answer: A substance made of different elements joined chemically

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.cause: Remembers "one kind" from the definition of an element and attaches it to the wrong word.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.reveals: Offer "A substance made of one kind of atom" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.help: Compare iron (one kind) and water (hydrogen and oxygen).
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.feedback: An element has one kind of atom. A compound has different elements joined.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.error: Says a compound is the same as a mixture.

example.question: How is a compound different from a mixture?
example.correct_answer: Its elements are joined chemically and cannot be separated easily

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.cause: Both a mixture and a compound have more than one substance in them, so the child sees no difference.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.reveals: Offer "It is not different" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.help: Try to separate iron filings from sand and then iron from iron sulphide.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.feedback: The elements in a compound are joined chemically. In a mixture they are only mixed.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.error: Gives the first letter of the name for every element (I for iron, S for sodium).

example.question: What is the symbol for iron?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.cause: Most symbols the child meets first (H, O, C, N) are the first letter, so the child makes it a rule.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.reveals: Offer "I" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.help: Some symbols come from old Latin names: ferrum for iron, natrium for sodium.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.feedback: Not every symbol is the first letter. Iron is Fe, sodium is Na and potassium is K.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.error: Reads K as calcium (or Ca as potassium), matching the symbol to an element whose name starts with the same sound.

example.question: Which element has the symbol K?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.cause: K sounds like the start of "calcium"; the Latin name kalium is not known.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.reveals: Offer "Calcium" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.help: Make a card for each symbol and its name.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.feedback: K is potassium. Calcium is Ca.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

example.question: Which word equation is correct?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.cause: Reads an equation like a sum written backwards, with the answer first.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.reveals: Offer "magnesium oxide gives magnesium + oxygen" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.help: Read the equation from the left: what we start with.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.feedback: The reactants come first, then an arrow, then the product.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.error: Gives the wrong name to the compound (iron sulphate for iron sulphide).

example.question: What is made when iron reacts with sulphur?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.cause: Has heard "sulphate" more often (on fertiliser bags) than "sulphide".
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.reveals: Offer "Iron sulphate" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.help: A compound of two elements ends in -ide.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.feedback: A compound of two elements has the ending -ide: iron sulphide, magnesium oxide, sodium chloride.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.error: Says the mass or the elements disappear in a reaction.

example.question: What happens to the atoms in a reaction?
example.correct_answer: They rearrange to make new substances

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.cause: Sees a solid burn away or a gas leave and thinks the matter has gone.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.reveals: Offer "They disappear" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.help: Weigh steel wool before and after it rusts.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.feedback: Atoms are not lost. They join in new ways to make new substances.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.error: Picks aluminium foil, not copper, as the element used for electric wires, because foil is a shiny metal at home.

example.question: Which element is used for electric wires?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.cause: Knows wires are metal and picks the metal seen most often in the kitchen.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.reveals: Offer "Aluminium foil" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.help: Match each element to an object at home.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.feedback: Copper is used for electric wires because it carries electricity well.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.error: Says packaging labels are only for decoration.

example.question: What does a packaging label tell you?
example.correct_answer: The contents, amounts and the date to use it by

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.cause: Has only looked at the picture and brand name on a packet.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.reveals: Offer "Nothing useful" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.feedback: Labels give contents, amounts, dates and safety information.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.error: Calls a compound such as water or salt an element.

example.question: Which of these is an element?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.cause: Water and salt are everyday "pure" things, so the child takes them to be single elements.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.reveals: Offer "Water" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.help: Ask what water is made of.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.feedback: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen. Oxygen is an element.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.error: Thinks a gas such as oxygen or nitrogen cannot be an element, because elements are solids like iron.

example.question: Is oxygen an element?
example.wrong_answer: No, elements are solids such as iron and copper
example.correct_answer: Yes: oxygen is made of one kind of atom

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.cause: Has met elements as metals first.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.reveals: Offer "No, elements are solids such as iron and copper" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.help: Sort a list (iron, oxygen, copper, nitrogen, water) by "one kind of atom or more".
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.feedback: An element can be a solid, a liquid or a gas. Oxygen is an element.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.AT.source: To confirm by a CBC Integrated Science teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.error: Writes both letters of a symbol as capitals (CU, NA) or the first as a small letter (fe).

example.question: How is the symbol for copper written?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.cause: Has not noticed that the second letter is small.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.reveals: Offer "CU" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.help: Show that CO is carbon monoxide (two elements) but Co is cobalt (one).
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.feedback: The first letter is a capital and the second is small: Cu, Na, Fe.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.source: To confirm by a CBC Integrated Science teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.error: Swaps the symbols for silver (Ag) and gold (Au).

example.question: What is the symbol for gold?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.cause: Both come from Latin names the child does not know and both start with A.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.reveals: Offer "Ag" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.help: Link them: Au is from aurum, gold; Ag is from argentum, silver.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.feedback: Gold is Au and silver is Ag.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.SY.source: To confirm by a CBC Integrated Science teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.error: Writes the product as the two element names joined with "and" (magnesium and oxygen) instead of the new compound.

example.question: Magnesium burns in oxygen. What is the product?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.cause: Thinks the reactants are still there side by side after the reaction.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.reveals: Offer "Magnesium and oxygen" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.help: Show burnt magnesium: a white powder, not the shiny metal and a gas.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.feedback: The product is a new substance with a new name: magnesium oxide.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.WO.source: Children's science research reports this idea (alternative conceptions literature). Cited from memory: verify the reference.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.error: Thinks chlorine is a food element because it is in table salt, so the gas is safe to breathe.

example.question: Chlorine is used to treat water. Is chlorine gas safe to breathe?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, it is in salt we eat
example.correct_answer: No: chlorine gas is toxic; in salt it is joined with sodium as a compound

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.cause: Does not see that a compound has different properties from its elements.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.reveals: Offer "Yes, it is in salt we eat" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.help: Compare the hazard label on a chlorine product with a salt packet.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.feedback: Chlorine gas is poisonous. In salt it is joined with sodium, which makes a safe compound.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.ELEMENTS_AND_COMPOUNDS.EL.source: To confirm by a CBC Integrated Science teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..error: Says the particles of a solid do not move at all.

example.question: How do the particles of a solid move?
example.wrong_answer: They do not move at all

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: A solid looks still, so the child thinks its particles are still.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "They do not move at all" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..help: Think of people standing in a queue who shake in place.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..feedback: Solid particles vibrate in fixed places. They do not move around.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..error: Says the particles of a gas are close together.

example.question: How far apart are the particles of a gas?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: Pictures a gas as a thick cloud, like smoke, rather than as empty space.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "Close together" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..help: Think of why a gas can be squeezed.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..feedback: Gas particles are far apart and move freely.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..error: Says the particles of a liquid are fixed in place.

example.question: How do the particles of a liquid move?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: Water in a glass looks still, and the child applies the solid picture to it.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "They stay in fixed places" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..help: Think of why a liquid takes the shape of its container.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..feedback: Liquid particles are close but slide past each other.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..error: Says impurities lower the boiling point.

example.question: What does salt do to the boiling point of water?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: Has heard that salt makes water cook food faster and takes that to mean it boils sooner.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "It lowers it" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..help: Boil pure water and salty water and compare the temperature.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..error: Says impurities raise the melting point.

example.question: What does an impurity do to the melting point of ice?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: Gives impurities the same effect on melting as on boiling.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "It raises it" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..help: Salt on icy roads helps ice to melt.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..feedback: Impurities lower the melting point, so salty water freezes below 0 degrees.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

example.question: Does salt change how water boils?
example.correct_answer: Yes, it boils at a higher temperature

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: A pinch of salt seems too small to change anything.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "No effect at all" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..feedback: Impurities change the boiling and melting points.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

example.question: Is melting ice a physical or chemical change?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: Melting looks like a big change, so the child calls it chemical.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "Chemical" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..help: Ask whether a new substance is made.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..feedback: Melting makes no new substance, so it is physical.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

example.question: Is burning wood a physical or chemical change?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: Sees burning as only a change of state (wood "melts" into smoke).
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "Physical" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..help: Ask whether the ash can turn back into wood.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..feedback: Burning makes new substances and cannot be reversed, so it is chemical.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..error: Says a physical change makes a new substance.

example.question: What does a chemical change make?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: Mixes up the two definitions taught side by side.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "No new substance" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..help: Compare dissolving sugar and burning sugar.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..feedback: A chemical change makes a new substance.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..error: Thinks the particles themselves get bigger when a substance is heated and expands.

example.question: A metal rod gets longer when heated. What happens to its particles?
example.correct_answer: The particles move more and take up more space; they do not get bigger

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: Sees the whole thing grow and gives the particles the same property.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "Each particle gets bigger" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..help: Act it out: learners shake harder and need more room, but stay the same size.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..feedback: When heated, particles move more and spread apart. They do not grow.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: Children's science research reports this idea (alternative conceptions literature). Cited from memory: verify the reference.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..error: Thinks a clear liquid must be pure, so its boiling point cannot show an impurity.

example.question: Two clear liquids boil at 100 degrees and 103 degrees. Which is pure water?
example.correct_answer: The one that boils at 100 degrees

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: Judges purity by how it looks.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "Either, they both look clear" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..help: Boil tap water and clear salty water side by side with a thermometer (teacher).
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..feedback: Pure water boils at 100 degrees at sea level. A different boiling point shows an impurity, even if it looks clear.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: To confirm by a CBC Integrated Science teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..error: Calls dissolving sugar in water a chemical change because the sugar seems to disappear.

example.question: Is dissolving sugar in tea a physical or a chemical change?
example.correct_answer: Physical: the sugar can be got back by evaporating the water

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..cause: Thinks "it vanished" means a new substance.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..reveals: Offer "Chemical, the sugar is gone" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..help: Evaporate sugar water on a saucer: sugar is left.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..feedback: Dissolving is a physical change. No new substance is made and the sugar can be got back.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.PHYSICAL_AND_CHEMICAL_CH..source: To confirm by a CBC Integrated Science teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.error: Says a fire needs only heat and fuel.

example.question: What three things does a fire need?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.cause: Oxygen cannot be seen, so the child leaves it out of the list.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.reveals: Offer "Heat and fuel only" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.help: Cover a burning candle with a jar.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.feedback: A fire needs heat, fuel and oxygen. Remove one and it goes out.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.error: Says water puts out every fire.

example.question: Which fire is NOT put out with water?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.cause: Has only seen wood fires put out with water.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.reveals: Offer "A wood fire" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.help: Ask why oil floats and spreads on water.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.feedback: Water spreads an oil fire. It is not used on oil or electrical fires.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.error: Gives a lit match (a human cause) when asked for a natural cause of fire, leaving out lightning and the sun on dry grass.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.error: Uses water on an oil fire.

example.question: What should you use on a cooking oil fire?
example.correct_answer: A damp cloth or a lid to cut off the air

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.help: Ask what water does to hot oil.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.feedback: Water makes an oil fire spread. Smother it.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.error: Uses water on an electrical fire.

example.question: What should you do first in an electrical fire?

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.cause: Does not link water with conducting electricity.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.reveals: Offer "Pour water on it" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.help: Ask why water and electricity are dangerous together.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.feedback: Switch off the power first. Never use water on an electrical fire.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.error: Tries to fight a large fire alone.

example.question: A fire is spreading fast. What should a child do?
example.correct_answer: Raise the alarm and get out safely

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.cause: Wants to help and does not know how fast a fire spreads.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.reveals: Offer "Fight it alone with water" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.feedback: Raise the alarm and leave safely. Only small fires are fought, by adults.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.error: Thinks fanning or blowing on a fire always puts it out.

example.question: Why does fanning a charcoal jiko make it burn brighter?
example.wrong_answer: It does not; fanning puts fires out

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.cause: Has blown out a match and generalises.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.reveals: Offer "It does not; fanning puts fires out" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.feedback: Fanning brings more oxygen, so a fire burns more. Blowing out a match takes away its heat.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_TRIA.source: To confirm by a CBC Integrated Science teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.cause: Has not seen the labels on extinguishers.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.reveals: Offer "Yes, any extinguisher works" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.help: Read the class labels on the school extinguisher.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.feedback: Each extinguisher is for certain classes of fire. Read the label before using it.
INTE.G8.MIXTUR.CLASSES_OF_FIRE.FIRE_CLAS.source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

example.question: Which cell has chloroplasts?

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.CELL_PARTS.M_G8_.reveals: Offer "An animal cell" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.CELL_PARTS.M_G8_.help: Ask which living things make their own food.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.CELL_PARTS.M_G8_.feedback: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.CELL_PARTS.M_G8_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.CELL_PARTS.M_G8_.error: Says the cell membrane only gives the cell its shape.

example.question: What does the cell membrane do?

example.correct_answer: Controls what enters and leaves the cell

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.CELL_PARTS.M_G8_.cause: Sees the membrane as the edge of the drawing, like a wall.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.CELL_PARTS.M_G8_.reveals: Offer "Gives the cell its shape only" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.CELL_PARTS.M_G8_.feedback: The membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.CELL_PARTS.M_G8_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.error: Adds the eyepiece and the objective magnifications.

example.question: The eyepiece is 10 times and the objective is 40 times. What is the total magnification?

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.cause: Uses addition because there are "two numbers to combine".
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.reveals: Offer "50 times" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.help: Look at each lens: the second lens magnifies the image of the first.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

example.question: The eyepiece is 10 times and the objective is 10 times. What is the total magnification?

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.cause: Looks only at the lens closest to the slide.

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.feedback: Both lenses magnify, so multiply: 10 times 10 is 100.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.error: Multiplies 10 by 40 and writes 40 or 140, losing the zero or adding instead.

example.question: What is 10 times 40?

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.cause: Slips in the multiplication by ten once the rule (multiply) is known.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.reveals: Offer "40" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.error: Thinks the magnification makes the cell itself bigger, rather than its image.

example.question: A cell looks 400 times bigger under a microscope. Has the cell grown?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, the microscope makes the cell bigger
example.correct_answer: No: only its image is bigger; the cell stays the same size

INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.cause: Talks about "making it bigger" and takes it literally.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.reveals: Offer "Yes, the microscope makes the cell bigger" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.help: Look at a printed letter e through a hand lens, then without it.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.feedback: A microscope makes an image bigger. The cell itself does not change size.
INTE.G8.LIVING.THE_CELL.MAGNIFICATION.M_.source: To confirm by a CBC Integrated Science teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..error: Says particles move from where they are few to where they are many.

example.question: In diffusion, particles move from...

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..cause: Thinks of particles "going to join the others", like people joining a crowd.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..reveals: Offer "Few to many" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..help: Open a bottle of perfume at the front of a room.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..feedback: Particles spread from where there are many to where there are few.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..error: Says osmosis is the movement of solutes.

example.question: What moves in osmosis?

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..cause: Since the salt is what is different, the child thinks it must be what moves.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..reveals: Offer "Dissolved salt" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..help: Soak a raisin and a dry bean.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..feedback: Osmosis is the movement of water through a membrane.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..error: Says diffusion needs energy from the cell.

example.question: Does diffusion need energy from the cell?

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..cause: Has learnt that living cells need energy for everything they do.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..reveals: Offer "Yes, always" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..help: Ask what makes the smell of cooking spread.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..feedback: Diffusion happens without the cell using energy.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..error: Says a potato strip in salty water goes soft because the salt goes into it, not because water leaves it.

example.question: A raw potato strip left in very salty water becomes soft and shorter. Why?
example.wrong_answer: Salt went into the potato and made it soft
example.correct_answer: Water moved out of the potato into the salty water by osmosis

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..cause: Sees salt as the thing that acts and does not picture water moving out.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..reveals: Offer "Salt went into the potato and made it soft" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..help: Weigh the strips before and after: the strip in salty water is lighter, so something left it.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..feedback: Water left the potato, so it became soft and shorter. In osmosis it is water that moves.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..error: Thinks a dye dropped into still water stays in one spot unless the water is stirred.

example.question: A drop of dye is put in a glass of still water and left. What happens after an hour?
example.wrong_answer: It stays as a drop at the bottom
example.correct_answer: The colour spreads through the water until it is even

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..cause: Has only seen colour spread when stirring.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..reveals: Offer "It stays as a drop at the bottom" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..help: Leave a drop of food colour in still water on a desk for a lesson and look every ten minutes.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..feedback: The dye spreads by itself by diffusion. Stirring only makes it faster.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..error: Predicts a raisin soaked in plain water will shrink.

example.question: A raisin is left in plain water overnight. What happens to it?
example.correct_answer: It swells, because water moves into it by osmosis

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..cause: Thinks water washes things away or dissolves them.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..reveals: Offer "It shrinks" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..help: Soak a raisin and a dry bean overnight and compare them with dry ones.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..feedback: Water moves into the raisin, where the sugar solution is stronger, so it swells.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..error: Thinks diffusion is faster in cold water than in hot water.

example.question: Dye is dropped into a cold glass and a hot glass of water. In which does it spread faster?
example.correct_answer: The hot glass: the particles move faster

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..cause: Has not linked temperature with how fast particles move.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..reveals: Offer "The cold glass" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..help: The teacher drops dye into warm and cold water side by side.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..feedback: Particles move faster when warm, so diffusion is faster in hot water.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..error: Thinks diffusion happens only in liquids, not in gases.

example.question: Does diffusion happen in air?
example.correct_answer: Yes: the smell of cooking spreads through a house by diffusion

INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..cause: Has seen diffusion taught with dye in water.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..reveals: Offer "No, only in water" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..help: Spray perfume at the front of the room and ask learners to raise a hand when they smell it.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..feedback: Diffusion happens in gases and liquids. Smells spread through air by diffusion.
INTE.G8.LIVING.MOVEMENT_OF_MATERIALS_IN..source: To confirm by a CBC Integrated Science teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..feedback: Menstruation is normal and not an illness.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..error: Says fertilisation happens in the uterus.

example.question: Which happens first?

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..cause: Has learnt the two words together without the order of events.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..reveals: Offer "Implantation" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..error: Says the zygote is the baby when it is born.

example.question: Which helps to prevent STIs?

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..cause: Thinks of an STI like dirt that can be washed off.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..reveals: Offer "Washing the body after sex" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..feedback: Abstinence and faithfulness to one uninfected partner prevent STIs.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..error: Thinks a girl should stay home from school during her period.

example.question: A girl starts her period at school. What is the best plan?
example.wrong_answer: Go home and stay away for the week
example.correct_answer: Use a pad (from her bag or the school nurse), carry on with school and tell a trusted adult if she needs help

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..cause: Has heard that periods mean missing school.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..reveals: Offer "Go home and stay away for the week" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..help: Plan with the class what a spare-pad kit and the school nurse can do.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..feedback: A period is no reason to miss school. Carry a spare pad and ask the school nurse or a trusted adult for help.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..error: Thinks one pad can be used for a whole day.

example.question: How often should a pad be changed?
example.correct_answer: Every four to six hours, or more often if bleeding is heavy

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..cause: Wants to save pads and does not know about germs and smell.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..reveals: Offer "Once a day" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..help: Talk about germs and skin irritation from a pad left too long.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..feedback: Change a pad every four to six hours to stay clean and healthy.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..error: Thinks very heavy bleeding or pain that stops a girl walking is normal and needs no health worker.

example.question: A girl has pain so bad she cannot walk, every month. What should she do?

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..cause: Has heard that cramps are normal and applies it to every pain.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..reveals: Offer "Nothing, all periods are painful" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..help: List signs that need a health worker: pain that stops daily life, very heavy bleeding, periods lasting more than a week.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..feedback: Some pain is common, but pain that stops you walking or very heavy bleeding needs a health worker.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..error: Thinks a girl must never talk to any adult about her period.

example.question: Who can a girl talk to about her period?
example.wrong_answer: No one, it must stay secret
example.correct_answer: A trusted adult: a parent, the school nurse or a female teacher

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..cause: Has learnt that periods are not talked about.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..reveals: Offer "No one, it must stay secret" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..help: Name trusted adults at home and at school with the class.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..feedback: It is good to talk to a trusted adult about periods. They can help.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..error: Thinks every girl's cycle is exactly 28 days from the start, so a shorter or irregular cycle means illness.

example.question: A 13-year-old's cycle is 25 days one month and 32 the next. Is she ill?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, it must be exactly 28 days
example.correct_answer: Not necessarily: cycles vary, especially in the first years; see a health worker if worried

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..cause: Takes the textbook number as a rule.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..reveals: Offer "Yes, it must be exactly 28 days" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..help: Explain that 28 days is an average; 21 to 35 days is common.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..feedback: 28 days is only an average. Cycles vary, especially when periods have just started.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..error: Thinks many sperm join one egg to make a baby.

example.question: How many sperm join the egg at fertilisation?

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..cause: Has heard that millions of sperm are released.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..reveals: Offer "Many sperm" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..help: Draw one sperm entering the egg; the egg then blocks the others.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..feedback: Only one sperm joins the egg to make the zygote.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..error: Thinks a person with no symptoms cannot have or pass on an STI.

example.question: Can a person with no signs of an STI pass it on?
example.correct_answer: Yes: some STIs show no signs for a long time; testing is the way to know

INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..reveals: Offer "No, they would have signs" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..help: Talk about testing at a health centre as the only way to know.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..feedback: Some STIs have no signs for a long time. Only a test at a health centre shows them.
INTE.G8.LIVING.REPRODUCTION_IN_HUMAN_BE..source: To confirm by a teacher or a health worker: a health or safety statement written for Grade 8.

example.question: Which is a renewable source?

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..cause: Coal is dug from the ground every year, so it seems to be always there.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..reveals: Offer "Coal" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..feedback: Coal is non-renewable. Sun, wind and flowing water are renewable.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..error: Calls solar or wind energy non-renewable.

example.question: Which is a non-renewable source?

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..cause: Thinks the sun or wind can "run out" on a cloudy or still day.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..reveals: Offer "Wind" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..help: Ask what is replaced by nature.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..feedback: Petroleum is non-renewable. Wind is renewable.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..error: Mixes up the forms of energy.

example.question: Which form of energy does a rolling ball have?

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..cause: Knows the names of the forms but not what each looks like in a real object.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..reveals: Offer "Chemical energy" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..help: Link the form with what the object is doing.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..error: Says an electric kettle changes electrical energy mainly into light (its indicator glows) rather than heat.

example.question: What does an electric kettle change electrical energy into?

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..cause: Notices the glowing light on the kettle and names what is seen.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..reveals: Offer "Light" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..help: Ask what the kettle gives out.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..feedback: A kettle changes electrical energy to heat.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..error: Says energy is created or used up.

example.question: What happens to energy when it is used?
example.wrong_answer: It is used up and disappears

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..cause: Everyday speech says batteries and fuel are "used up".
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..reveals: Offer "It is used up and disappears" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..help: Follow the energy of a falling stone.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..feedback: Energy is never created or used up. It changes form.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..error: Gives sound or heat, not electrical energy, as what a solar panel changes light into.

example.question: What does a solar panel change light into?

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..cause: Has seen solar radios and solar heaters and names their end use.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..reveals: Offer "Sound" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..help: Link a solar lamp to the sun.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..feedback: A solar panel changes light to electrical energy.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..error: Does not see food as a store of chemical energy.

example.question: What form of energy is stored in a plate of ugali?

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..cause: Thinks of energy as electricity or movement only.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..reveals: Offer "None, food is not energy" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..help: Link food to activity: after eating we can run and keep warm.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..feedback: Food stores chemical energy. The body changes it into movement and heat.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..source: To confirm by a CBC Integrated Science teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..error: Gives only one change when there is a chain, for example a torch changes chemical energy straight into light.

example.question: Write the energy changes in a torch.
example.correct_answer: Chemical to electrical to light (and some heat)

INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..cause: Skips the middle step that cannot be seen.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..reveals: Offer "Chemical to light" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..help: Follow the torch: battery, wire, bulb; name the energy at each.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..feedback: Many devices change energy in steps. A torch: chemical, then electrical, then light and heat.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.TRANSFORMATION_OF_ENERGY..source: To confirm by a CBC Integrated Science teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.error: Says pressure depends only on the force.

example.question: The same force acts on a small area and a large area. Where is the pressure bigger?

INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.cause: Thinks of pressure as the same as pushing, so only the size of the push matters.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.reveals: Offer "The same in both" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.help: Press a finger and a nail into soft clay.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.feedback: The same force on a smaller area gives a bigger pressure.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.error: Says a larger area gives more pressure.

example.question: Why do wide tyres sink less in mud?

INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.cause: Thinks a bigger thing must press harder.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.reveals: Offer "They give more pressure" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.help: Compare walking in boots and in snow shoes.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.feedback: A larger area spreads the force, so the pressure is smaller.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.error: Says pressure in a liquid stays the same with depth.

example.question: How does liquid pressure change with depth?

INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.cause: Thinks water is the same everywhere in a tank, so its push is too.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.reveals: Offer "It stays the same" next to the right answer in a new question and ask the child to choose.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.help: Poke holes at different heights in a bottle.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.feedback: Liquid pressure grows with depth, so a dam wall is thicker at the bottom.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.error: Thinks a wider tank of water gives more pressure at the bottom than a narrow one of the same depth.

example.question: Two tanks of water are both 2 m deep; one is wide and one narrow. Where is the pressure at the bottom bigger?
example.wrong_answer: In the wide tank, it holds more water
example.correct_answer: The same in both: liquid pressure depends on depth, not width

INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.cause: Thinks more water means more pressure.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.reveals: Offer "In the wide tank, it holds more water" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.help: Fill a wide and a narrow bottle to the same height, with a hole at the same low point: the jets go the same distance.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.feedback: Liquid pressure depends on depth, not on how much water there is.
INTE.G8.FORCE_.PRESSURE.PRESSURE.M_G8_PR.source: Children's science research reports this idea (alternative conceptions literature). Cited from memory: verify the reference.
